1 Case :- CRIMINAL MISC. BAIL APPLICATION No. - 39105 of 2023 Applicant :- Gaurav Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others Counsel for Applicant :- Chandra Shekhar Mishra Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Rajeev Misra,J.
1.

Heard Mr. A.K.S. Bais, the learned counsel for applicant-Anand Kumar, Mr. Avinash Pandey, the learned counsel for applicant-Gaurav, Mr. Chandra Shekhar Mishra, the learned counsel for another applicant-Gaurav and the learned A.G.A. for State.
2. Perused the record.
3. Present applications for bail came up for orders on 05.10.2023 and this Court passed the following order:-
"Heard Mr. Ashok Kumar Singh Bais, the learned counsel for applicant and the learned A.G.A. for State.
Perused the record.

This application for bail has been filed by applicant Anand Kumar, seeking his enlargement on bail in Case Crime No. 86 of 2023, under Section 376-D.A, 506 IPC and Section 5-G/6 POCSO Act, Section 67-A I.T. Act Police Station- Nagal, District Saharanpur during the pendency of trial.
At the very outset, learned A.G.A. submits that notice of present application for bail has been served upon opposite party-2 on 12.6.2023.
However, inspite of service of notice, no one has put in appearance on behalf of first informant-opposite party-2 to oppose this application for bail.

After some arguments, it appears that the age of the prosecutrix has been determined as per date of birth of the prosecutrix i.e. 25.10.2009, mentioned in the School Leaving Certificate dated 3.4.2023.
As such, prosecutrix is said to be aged about 13 years and four months and 16 days on the date of occurrence i.e. 11.3.2023.

Prima faice the determination of age made on the basis of the date of birth of the prosecutrix recorded in the School Leaving Certificate is not tenable in law by virtue Anand Kumar vs State Of U.P.And 3 Others on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125053114/
2 of Section 94 of the Juvenile Justice (care and protection) Act.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The age of the prosecutrix could have been determined only in accordance with date of birth of the prosecutrix as per documents recognized under Section 94(1)(a) and 94 (1)(b) of the Juvenile Justice (care and protection) Act.
Similar view has been taken by the Apex Court in the case of P. Yuvaprakash Vs. State, 2023 Live Law (SC) 538.

entities.text: P. Yuvaprakash Vs. State, 2023 Live Law (SC) 538
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned A.G.A. submits that charge sheet has already been submitted against applicant on 28.4.2023.
After some arguments, it transpires that the age of the prosecutrix has been determined as per her date of birth i.e. 25.10.2009 recorded in the School Leaving Certificate dated 3.4.2003.

In view of the fact that police report in terms of Section 173 (2) Cr.P.C. has been submitted against applicants on 28.4.2023, therefore, the Investigating Officer is directed to submit an application before court concerned in terms of Section 173 (8)
Cr.P.C. seeking permission of the Court to conduct further investigation.

After obtaining permission of the court, Investigating Officer shall conduct further investigation to find out the date of birth of the prosecutrix recorded in the institution which was first attended by her.
The necessary exercise shall be undertaken by the Investigating Officer within a period of three weeks from today.
Copy of supplementary case diary shall also be transmitted to this Court through the learned A.G.A. before the next date fixed.
Matter shall accordingly reappear as fresh on 1.11.2023.
Subsequent to above order, the learned A.G.A. has filed an affidavit on behalf of the Investigating Officer, which is already on record.

5. Record shows that in respect of an incident, which is alleged to have occurred on 11.03.2023, a delayed FIR dated 05.04.2023 was lodged by first informant-Babita (mother of the prosecutrix) and was registered as Case Crime No. 0086 of 2023, under Sections 376-D, 506 IPC and Sections 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station-Nagal, District-Saharanpur.

In the aforesaid FIR, 4 persons namely (1)
Anand (2) Yogesh, (3) Gaurav and (4) Gaurav have been nominated as named accused.

5. The gravamen of the allegations made in the FIR is to the effect that named accused deliberately and forcefully dislodged the modesty of the daughter of the first informant i.e. the prosecutrix namely X aged about 15 years.
6. After above-mentioned FIR was lodged, Investigating Officer proceeded with statutory investigation of concerned case crime number in terms of Chapter-XII Cr.P.C.
The statement of the prosecutrix was recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C.

Same is on record at page 21 of the bail Anand Kumar vs State Of U.P.And 3 Others on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125053114/
3 application of applicant-Anand Kumar.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The prosecutrix in her aforesaid statement has not only supported the FIR but has also detailed the manner of occurrence.
Apart from the allegation that her modesty was dislodged, the prosecutrix has further alleged that named accused prepared an obscene video of the occurrence.
Thereafter, the prosecutrix was requested for her internal medical examination.
The prosecutrix in her statement before the Doctor, who medically examined her, has reiterated her previous statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C.
The same is evident from the document occurring at page 32 of the bail application of applicant-Anand Kumar.
The Doctor, who medically examined the prosecutrix, did not find any injury on her person so as to denote commission of deliberate and forceful sexual assault.
It is worth noticing that the Medico Legal Examination of the prosecutrix was conducted after 25 days of the occurrence.

However, with regard to the private part of the prosecutrix, the Doctor has opined as under:-
"Hymen Perinseum Old torned"
7.
Certain samples were collected from the body of prosecutrix for pathological examination.
However, the results of the same are in negative.
Ultimately, the statement of the prosecutrix was recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
Same is on record at page 50 of the paper book pertaining to applicant-Anand Kumar.

The prosecutrix in her aforesaid statement has fully reiterated her previous statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C.
8.

During course of investigation, Investigating Officer recovered the School Leaving Certificate of the prosecutrix dated 03.04.2023 wherein the date of birth of the prosecutrix is mentioned as 25.10.2009.
The occurrence giving rise to present criminal proceedings occurred on 11.03.2023.
As such, the prosecutrix was aged about 13 years, 4 months and 16 days on the date of occurrence.
Investigating Officer also examined the first informant (mother of the prosecutrix) and other witnesses under Section 161 Cr.P.C.
Witnesses so examined have supported the FIR.
Investigating Officer further recovered the obscene video prepared by the named accused and made viral from the mobile phone of the first informant.
The first informant has further submitted the requisite certificate under Section 65-B of the Evidence Act.

On the basis of above and other material collected by Investigating Officer during course of investigation, he came to the conclusion that complicity of named accused is established in the crime in question.
He, accordingly, submitted the charge sheet dated 28.04.2023 whereby all the named accused have been charge sheeted under Sections 376-DA, 506 IPC, Sections 5G/6 POCSO Act and Section 67-A I.T. Act.
9. Learned counsel for applicants contend that though applicants are named as well as charge sheeted accused yet they are liable to be enlarged on bail.

Attention of the Court was invited to the Medico Legal Examination Report of the prosecutrix and on basis thereof, it is urged that medical evidence does not support the ocular version of the occurrence inasmuch as, no signs were found on the body of the prosecutrix denoting commission of deliberate and forceful sexual assault.
10. It is then contended by the learned counsel for applicants that applicants and the prosecutrix belong to the same village.
The applicants have been falsely implicated in the crime in question on account of petty politics.

Anand Kumar vs State Of U.P.And 3 Others on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125053114/
4 11.

entities.text: Anand Kumar vs State Of U.P.And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even otherwise, applicants are men of clean antecedents inasmuch as, they have no criminal history to their credit except the present one.
Applicants-Anand Kumar and Gaurav are in jail since 06.04.2023 whereas the another applicant-Gaurav is in jail since 24.04.2023.
As such, they have undergone substantial periods of incarceration.

The police report in terms of Section 173(2) Cr.P.C.
has already been submitted.
As such, the entire evidence sought to be relied upon by the prosecution against applicants stands crystallized.
However, up to this stage, no such circumstance has emerged necessitating the custodial arrest of applicants during the pendency of trial.
On the above premise, it is urged that applicants are liable to be enlarged on bail.

In case, the applicants are enlarged on bail,
they shall not misuse the liberty of bail and shall co-operate with the trial.
12. Per contra, the learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail.
He submits that since applicants are named and charge sheeted accused, therefore, they do not deserve any indulgence by this Court.
The prosecutrix is a young girl aged about 13 years, 4 months and 16 days on the basis of her date of birth recorded in the School Leaving Certificate.
Learned A.G.A. has then referred to the affidavit of compliance dated 31.10.2023 filed by the Investigating Officer.

With reference to above, he submits that as per the certificate issued by the Principal of the institution where the prosecutrix studied from Class-3 to Class-5, her date of birth recorded in the institution is 25.10.2009.

It is thus urged by the learned A.G.A. that since the prosecutrix was below 16 years of age and the applicants are guilty of dislodging the modesty of the girl, who is in tender age, therefore, they do not deserve any sympathy of this Court.

According to the learned A.G.A., the prosecutrix in her statements under Sections 161/164 Cr.P.C. and before the Doctor has not only supported the FIR but has also detailed the manner of occurrence in categorical terms.
The medical opinion given by the Doctor, who medically examined the prosecutrix, regarding her private parts clearly corroborates the ocular version of the occurrence.
As such, no sympathy be shown by this Court in favour of applicants.
13. When confronted with above, the learned counsel for applicants could not overcome the same.

14. Having heard, the learned counsel for applicants, the learned A.G.A. for State, upon perusal of record, evidence, nature and gravity of offence, complicity of accused, accusations made coupled with the fact that the prosecutrix in her statements under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. and in her statement before the Doctor has remained clear, categorical and consistent, she has not only supported the FIR but has also detailed the manner of occurrence, it is true that as per the medical evidence, no signs were found on the body of the prosecutrix to denote the commission of deliberate sexual assault but this fact cannot be lost sight of that the prosecutrix was medically examined after 25 days of the occurrence,, the opinion expressed by the Medical Officer regarding the private part of the prosecutrix clearly supports the FIR and corroborates the statement of the prosecutrix, since the prosecutrix is below 16 years of age as per the date of birth available, therefore, no sympathy can be shows by this Court in favour of applicants, in view of law laid down by the Apex Curt in X (Minor) Vs. The State of Jharkhand and Another 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 194, it is now well setteled that the prosecution of an accused for an offence of rape or sexual assault can be maintained even in the absence of medical evidence and on the solitary statement of the prosecutrix vide lay laid down by the Apex Court in Phool Singh Vs. State of M.P., (2022) 2 SCC 74, when the statements of the prosecutrix referred to above are examined as a whole, the same fall in the category of impeccable evidence, as they are devoid of exaggeration, embellishment or contradiction, up to this stage, there Anand Kumar vs State Of U.P.And 3 Others on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125053114/
5 is no such material on the basis of which, the prosecution story can be said to be false or nor it can be inferred that applicants are being falsely and maliciously prosecuted in the crime in question,
therefore, irrespective of the varied submissions urged by the learned counsel for applicants in support of the present applications for bail, but without making any comments on the merits of the case, this Court does not find any good or sufficient ground to enlarge the applicants on bail.

16. They are, accordingly, rejected.
